3:1.sourceText: Ἐν δὲ ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις παραγίνεται Ἰωάνης ὁ βαπτιστὴς κηρύσσων ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τῆς Ἰουδαίας,
3:1.targetText: And in those days John the Immerser comes, proclaiming in the wilderness of Judea,

groups.note: The actual βαπτιστής designation is rendered Immerser by LSV; the source keeps that Baptist/immersing-agent noun, not a newly invented different Greek title.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with those days.

3:2.sourceText: λέγων Μετανοεῖτε· ἤγγικεν γὰρ ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.
3:2.targetText: and saying, “Convert, for the kingdom of the heavens has come near,”

groups.note: The actual change-of-mind/repentance imperative μετανοεῖτε is rendered Convert by LSV. The link exposes that repentance head rather than inventing a different Greek turn/convert verb.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV follows an added and before saying; pinned N1904 begins with the saying participle without that conjunction.

3:3.sourceText: οὗτος γάρ ἐστιν ὁ ῥηθεὶς διὰ Ἠσαΐου τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος Φωνὴ βοῶντος ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ Ἑτοιμάσατε τὴν ὁδὸν Κυρίου, εὐθείας ποιεῖτε τὰς τρίβους αὐτοῦ.
3:3.targetText:
for this is he having been spoken of by Isaiah the prophet, saying, “A voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the LORD,
Make His paths straight.”

groups.note: The actual genitive crying participle is substantival and identifies whose voice it is, rendered of one crying. One is English nominal support, not a separately printed Greek numeral.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with His paths.

3:4.sourceText: Αὐτὸς δὲ ὁ Ἰωάνης εἶχεν τὸ ἔνδυμα αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τριχῶν καμήλου καὶ ζώνην δερματίνην περὶ τὴν ὀσφὺν αὐτοῦ· ἡ δὲ τροφὴ ἦν αὐτοῦ ἀκρίδες καὶ μέλι ἄγριον.
3:4.targetText: And this John had his clothing of camel’s hair, and a girdle of skin around his loins, and his nourishment was locusts and honey of the field.

groups.note: Greek αὐτός emphasizes John himself; LSV identifies him as this John. The same emphatic personal reference is retained with that rendering explicit, without relabeling the source as the different Greek demonstrative οὗτος.
The actual leather/skin adjective is rendered by the English genitive of skin; no separate Greek skin noun is invented.
The actual wild adjective ἄγριον qualifies honey; LSV expresses it as of the field. The English noun-genitive phrase is the rendering of that adjective, not a separately printed Greek field noun.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles have no separately expressed English word with John or the possessive clothing, loins and nourishment phrases.

3:5.sourceText: Τότε ἐξεπορεύετο πρὸς αὐτὸν Ἱεροσόλυμα καὶ πᾶσα ἡ Ἰουδαία καὶ πᾶσα ἡ περίχωρος τοῦ Ἰορδάνου,
3:5.targetText: Then were going forth to him Jerusalem, and all Judea, and all the region around the Jordan,

groups.note: The Greek going-out imperfect is third-person singular with the collective place-name subject; LSV uses plural were going forth for Jerusalem and the coordinated regions. The actual movement predicate is retained with that English agreement explicit.
The actual surrounding-region noun is rendered region around, with its own surrounding sense supplying around; no extra Greek around preposition is invented.
The actual Greek Jordan genitive identifies the surrounding region; English gives the Jordan directly after around. The complete case-marked name phrase retains that regional relationship.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with the place name Judea.

3:6.sourceText: καὶ ἐβαπτίζοντο ἐν τῷ Ἰορδάνῃ ποταμῷ ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ ἐξομολογούμενοι τὰς ἁμαρτίας αὐτῶν.
3:6.targetText: and they were immersed in the Jordan by him, confessing their sins.

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 explicitly names river with the Jordan; displayed LSV has only the Jordan and no separate river noun.
The Greek article is not separately expressed with their sins.

3:7.sourceText: Ἰδὼν δὲ πολλοὺς τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ Σαδδουκαίων ἐρχομένους ἐπὶ τὸ βάπτισμα εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Γεννήματα ἐχιδνῶν, τίς ὑπέδειξεν ὑμῖν φυγεῖν ἀπὸ τῆς μελλούσης ὀργῆς;
3:7.targetText: And having seen many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming about his immersion, he said to them, “Brood of vipers! Who showed you to flee from the coming wrath?

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with the English possessive his immersion.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV explicitly adds his with immersion; N1904 has only the definite immersion phrase, without a possessive pronoun.

3:8.sourceText: ποιήσατε οὖν καρπὸν ἄξιον τῆς μετανοίας·
3:8.targetText: Bear, therefore, fruits worthy of conversion,

groups.note: N1904 writes singular fruit, καρπόν, while LSV prints plural fruits. The actual fruit noun is retained with this source/English number difference explicit.
The actual repentance/change-of-mind noun μετάνοια is rendered conversion by LSV; the correspondence keeps that written head, not a different Greek turning noun.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with conversion.

3:9.sourceText: καὶ μὴ δόξητε λέγειν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς Πατέρα ἔχομεν τὸν Ἀβραάμ· λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι δύναται ὁ Θεὸς ἐκ τῶν λίθων τούτων ἐγεῖραι τέκνα τῷ Ἀβραάμ.
3:9.targetText: and do not think to say in yourselves, We have a father—Abraham, for I say to you that God is able to raise children to Abraham out of these stones,

groups.note: The actual second-person thinking subjunctive forms the prohibition under μή; the English command auxiliary do belongs to this verbal predicate, while not retains the separate written negator.
The actual dative Abraham phrase identifies the recipient/father of the raised children, rendered to Abraham; no standalone Greek to preposition is invented.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles have no separately expressed English word with Abraham, God or these stones.

3:10.sourceText: ἤδη δὲ ἡ ἀξίνη πρὸς τὴν ῥίζαν τῶν δένδρων κεῖται· πᾶν οὖν δένδρον μὴ ποιοῦν καρπὸν καλὸν ἐκκόπτεται καὶ εἰς πῦρ βάλλεται.
3:10.targetText: and now also, the axe is laid to the root of the trees, therefore, every tree not bearing good fruit is cut down, and is cast into fire.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV follows an additional also at the opening; pinned N1904 has now/already and the connective but/and, without a separate additive καί.

3:11.sourceText: ἐγὼ μὲν ὑμᾶς βαπτίζω ἐν ὕδατι εἰς μετάνοιαν· ὁ δὲ ὀπίσω μου ἐρχόμενος ἰσχυρότερός μού ἐστιν, οὗ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἱκανὸς τὰ ὑποδήματα βαστάσαι· αὐτὸς ὑμᾶς βαπτίσει ἐν Πνεύματι Ἁγίῳ καὶ πυρί·
3:11.targetText: I indeed immerse you in water for conversion, but He who is coming after me is mightier than I, of whom I am not worthy to carry the sandals, He will immerse you in the Holy Spirit and fire,

groups.note: The Greek first-person genitive marks the comparison standard with mightier; English expresses that actual case-governed relation as than I. The genitive is not falsely presented as an independent nominative I or a separate Greek than preposition.
The actual sufficient/fit adjective ἱκανός is rendered worthy in the service-fitness context; the source is not silently changed to the distinct adjective ἄξιος.

3:12.sourceText: οὗ τὸ πτύον ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ διακαθαριεῖ τὴν ἅλωνα αὐτοῦ, καὶ συνάξει τὸν σῖτον αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν ἀποθήκην, τὸ δὲ ἄχυρον κατακαύσει πυρὶ ἀσβέστῳ.
3:12.targetText: whose fan [is] in His hand, and He will thoroughly cleanse His floor, and will gather His wheat into the storehouse, but He will burn the chaff with unquenchable fire.”

groups.note: The actual dative fire noun gives the instrument of burning, rendered with ... fire; the case-governed noun phrase supplies with without a separate Greek preposition.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles have no separately expressed English word with whose fan or the possessive hand, floor and wheat phrases.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula in the Greek verbless whose-fan-in-His-hand clause; no corresponding Greek be verb is written.

3:13.sourceText: Τότε παραγίνεται ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας ἐπὶ τὸν Ἰορδάνην πρὸς τὸν Ἰωάνην τοῦ βαπτισθῆναι ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ.

3:14.sourceText: ὁ δὲ διεκώλυεν αὐτὸν λέγων Ἐγὼ χρείαν ἔχω ὑπὸ σοῦ βαπτισθῆναι, καὶ σὺ ἔρχῃ πρός με;

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article functions as the implicit male subject of forbidding; LSV explicitly names John instead of retaining a personal pronoun at this point.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV explicitly names John in the forbidding clause; N1904 has the articular personal subject without a written John name.

3:15.sourceText: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἄφες ἄρτι· οὕτως γὰρ πρέπον ἐστὶν ἡμῖν πληρῶσαι πᾶσαν δικαιοσύνην. τότε ἀφίησιν αὐτόν.

3:16.sourceText: βαπτισθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εὐθὺς ἀνέβη ἀπὸ τοῦ ὕδατος· καὶ ἰδοὺ ἠνεῴχθησαν οἱ οὐρανοί, καὶ εἶδεν Πνεῦμα Θεοῦ καταβαῖνον ὡσεὶ περιστερὰν ἐρχόμενον ἐπ’ αὐτόν·

3:17.sourceText: καὶ ἰδοὺ φωνὴ ἐκ τῶν οὐρανῶν λέγουσα Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός, ἐν ᾧ εὐδόκησα.
